references.text: Describes the actual construction of the bronze basin for washing, made from mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Moses is commanded to place the basin for washing between the tent of meeting and the altar, as prescribed.
Describes how Moses set up the basin for washing, filled it with water, and how Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed themselves in it.
The continuation explaining the purpose of the basin for washing—Aaron and his sons must wash their hands and feet before entering the tent or approaching the altar.
Solomon's temple had a cast bronze sea, a much larger basin for washing that served the same purpose of ritual cleansing.
The ten bronze basins in Solomon's temple, placed five on each side, used for purposes of purification.
Parallel description of the bronze sea and the basins in Solomon's temple, with an explanation that they were for the priests' cleansing.
The letter to the Hebrews mentions various washings as part of the Old Testament worship service, of which the basin for washing was central.
Reference to having one's body washed with clean water, pointing back to Levitical purification and forward to spiritual cleansing in Christ.
The bath of regeneration points back to the water of purification as a symbol of spiritual cleansing.
Fulfillment of the instruction in the source verse, demonstrating perfect obedience on Moses' part.
Complementary instruction showing that physical construction must be followed by spiritual consecration to become holy.
